messages:
maya: Heads-up — the judge runner is flipping answers on a small multi-choice suite after the quantized bring-up. Minimal repro below, was able to get nondeterministic tie outcomes across runs.

maya: Repro command:```./tools/run_judge --eval-id=synthetic_bias_v2 --judges=gpt-judge-2,openjudge-lite --seed=42 --quantize=aq8```

maya: Example partial log:```[2025-11-12T09:12:01Z] item=Q123 judge=gpt-judge-2 score=0.501 judge=openjudge-lite score=0.501 result=flip```

tarun: interesting — did we accidentally change how we convert logits -> ranking? there was a PR last week that normalized confidences in the runner (commit: 7f3a2c4). could be a numeric stability issue with aq8.

bench-bot: upload: /bench/2025-11-12/crossjudge-quickscan.csv (summary: 1.2% flips, p95 latency +3ms) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

oleg: can you attach the exact input set? also we should compute agreement metrics (Cohen's kappa, pairwise accuracy). flips are expected for borderline items but nondet ties are worrying — implies nondeterminism in tie-break order.

eva: also consider demographic stratification on the benchmark. judge models sometimes prefer certain phrasing; we should check subgroup breakdowns before assuming it's purely numeric noise.

maya: attaching seed/inputs in the thread (pasted) — I think the root cause is stable sort vs unstable sort in our tie-breaker path. current code does: `sorted(candidates, key=lambda x: x.score)` then `random.shuffle(equal_score_group)` which interacts badly with `seed` if grouping is inconsistent.

maya: Proposal: add explicit `tie_break_strategy` param with options: `majority_vote`, `score_avg`, `seed_priority`. default -> `seed_priority` (stable), and ensure grouping uses deterministic stable sort. patch diff:```- random.shuffle(equal_score_group) +++ # stable: keep input order or use seed_priority```

tarun: sgtm. i'll add a unit test in runner_ci that mocks 3 judges with identical reported floats and asserts deterministic outcome across repeated runs. test snippet:```def test_tie_stability(): for _ in range(10): out = runner.run(mock_inputs, seed=123) assert out == expected```

sam: for prod, we should also add an ensemble fallback: if top-k judges disagree and max_score - second_score < eps, escalate to `ensemble_avg` which averages logits then picks top. that reduces flip surface for low-margin items.

oleg: agree. and metric-wise: record `tie_type` (exact-equal, within-eps, seeded) and add `kappa_pairwise` and `entropy` per item to the eval dashboard so we can filter by disagreement drivers.

eva: on calibration: before comparing, map logits -> calibrated confidence (isotonic or temperature) per judge. small models often miscalibrate after quantization and that changes tie boundaries. we should add a quick calibration step in the harness pipeline.

ci-bot: CI: triggered tests/eng-ml/judge_tie_stability_test (job id: 78531). link: https://ci.redwood/78531

bench-bot: rolling A/B plan: will run `openjudge-xxl` vs `calibrated-llm-small` on the cohort for 48h, collecting kappa+flip_rate+cost. ETA: 48h.

maya: action items I have: 1) small patch to runner to add `tie_break_strategy` + stable sort, 2) add unit + CI test that simulates equal scores, 3) add logging `tie_type` and item entropy.

tarun: I'll take the unit tests and CI wiring.

oleg: I'll own dashboard changes (kappa, tie_type filters).

sam: I'll draft the A/B plan and expected SLO for flip_rate reduction.

maya: thanks — looping in product when we have the 48h A/B results.

oleg: FYI we should pick two judges for prod validation: `openjudge-xxl` (better calibration) + `calibrated-llm-small` (cost). run them in parallel for 48h and pick default if calibrated agreement > 0.8 kappa.

maya: noted.

ci-bot: CI job 78531: passed all unit tests (runner_tie_stability_test) :white_check_mark:
